lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Check that the profile link works and shows relevant product work.
items.because: The link should give a useful view of your product experience.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not needed to assess your qualifications and introduces irrelevant personal information.

items.says: Usually remove nationality for U.S. applications.
items.because: It is generally unnecessary unless an application requests relevant work-authorization information.

items.says: Make the MBA’s completion status clear when you apply.
items.because: The degree status should be accurate.

items.says: Give the older degree less visual emphasis if space is tight.
items.because: The MBA and experience are more important to emphasize.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% increase is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: The size of the conversion improvement is ambiguous.

items.says: Specify the measurement period and comparison for the conversion claim.
items.because: They need to support the reported improvement.

items.says: Verify the claim that the change applied to all merchants.
items.because: That is a broad scope claim that should be literally accurate.

items.says: Show the feature’s user, support, or business outcome if available.
items.because: The bullet emphasizes coordination and shipping ahead of plan more than impact.

items.says: Clarify your specific contribution to the dispute self-service launch.
items.because: The bullet emphasizes the team’s work.

items.says: Specify the currency for the 1.1 million-dollar estimate.
items.because: The amount does not identify a currency.

items.says: Make clear how the chargeback-loss estimate was annualized.
items.because: The bullet calls it an annual estimate.

items.says: Substantiate the claim that your analysis set the roadmap priority.
items.because: Your work should have materially informed that decision.

items.says: Use consistent U.S. English for “analysed.”
items.because: The roles and contact details suggest U.S. applications.

items.says: Clarify whether you or the team closed the 140 tickets.
items.because: Ownership of the ticket closures is ambiguous.

items.says: Explain how the queue reduction was measured.
items.because: The scope of the reported reduction is unclear.

items.says: Add the comparison’s finding or impact, or remove the bullet.
items.because: It states a method but no result.

items.says: Acknowledge the opt-in comparison’s limits.
items.because: Opt-in merchants may differ from nonparticipants, so the comparison alone may not establish causation.

items.says: Move the onboarding outcome earlier in the internship.
items.because: It is one of the role’s strongest, most relevant results.

items.says: Clarify that the 2,300 merchants were in the pilot region.
items.because: The scope of the result should be clear.

items.says: Explain whether the first-payment times use comparable measurements.
items.because: The reported reduction needs a sound comparison.

items.says: Excluding weather delays changes the late-delivery metric rather than demonstrating improved service.
items.because: The bullet presents the adjusted figure as a reduction in late deliveries.

items.says: Clarify the pick-error measurement period or scale.
items.because: It would give the 30% reduction more context.

items.says: Check that pick errors have the same definition before and after the change.
items.because: The reduction needs a consistent measure.

items.says: “Prepares” shifts to present tense.
items.because: The other bullets describe completed work.

items.says: Add the S&OP review’s scope, supported decision, or result.
items.because: The bullet reads as a responsibility rather than an outcome.

items.says: Say whether the annual driver-hour savings were measured or forecast.
items.because: That distinction matters to credibility.

items.says: Clarify the period meant by “in its first year.”
items.because: The project is listed as ongoing.

items.says: Clarify the baseline and measurement period for weekly active users.
items.because: The increase needs measurement context.

items.says: Avoid implying the reminders alone caused user growth without evidence.
items.because: The reported growth followed the change but may not have been caused by it.

items.says: Define what the 95% pickup-slot figure measures.
items.because: The measure is unclear.

items.says: Clarify the period and attribution of the drop in staff cover shifts.
items.because: The review asks whether it is weekly and due to the new system.

items.says: Explain your contribution to the working sessions.
items.because: The bullet shows stakeholder contact but not what you contributed.

items.says: Add a concrete project output or impact.
items.because: The bullet does not say what changed as a result.

items.says: Use active wording that makes your role clear.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your contribution.

items.says: Quantify how much the intake form was shortened.
items.because: “Shortened” gives no measure.

items.says: Give an observed result of the intake changes if available.
items.because: Adoption by staff does not show whether the changes helped.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result duplicates the Harbor achievement.
items.because: It strongly resembles an accidental paste.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding claim is misplaced in the hospital practicum.
items.because: The wording gives no clear reason it belongs to that project.

items.says: Substantiate the A/B-testing skill or remove it.
items.because: The résumé shows an observational opt-in comparison, not necessarily a randomized experiment.

items.says: Give more indication of your level or use of the listed tools.
items.because: The tools section is short and provides neither.

items.says: Consider a brief target-specific summary or headline.
items.because: Readers currently have to infer the transition from operations to product work.

items.says: Make the skills section more specific and evidence-based.
items.because: Its labels are broad and could read as unsubstantiated keywords.

items.says: Standardize date style, punctuation, and number and unit formatting.
items.because: The review calls for consistency throughout.

items.says: Check length and visual hierarchy in the final document.
items.because: The supplied text does not show page breaks or layout.

items.says: Keep projects from crowding out paid work.
items.because: An early-career product résumé should make its strongest experience easy to scan.
